correctness.rationale: In the 3-agent homogeneous irreversible-infection asynchronous best-response process with 0<a<1 and a/2<tau<min(a,1/2), the first update event and subsequent independent uniform first-appearance races partition all trajectories. Infected initial vertex chosen first (prob 1/3) yields one survivor phase iff tau>=theta1=a/(1+a); otherwise all infected. If a susceptible is chosen first (2/3), next two-label race is fair; one survivor after agent1 update requires tau>=theta0=(sqrt(1+8a)-1)/4 and the remaining susceptible to be updated next (prob 1/3). A further two-race exceptional event requires tau>=theta2=(sqrt(a^2+8a)-a)/4, giving contribution 1/18. Hence P(K=1)=1/3 indicator(tau>=theta1), P(K=2)=1/9 indicator(tau>=theta0)+1/18 indicator(tau>=theta2), and all remaining mass K=3. Equality is safe because infection is strict >tau. Independent rational 17-epoch Markov state propagation checked exact probability enclosures for seven parameter pairs including threshold boundaries, with unresolved tail about 0.001015 each; these are finite-horizon corroboration, not proof of infinite-time convergence.
